business_problem: Wattsense needed a low-overhead database that could ingest building-sensor data, device configurations, and metadata at scale while supporting rapid iteration, reliable operations, and efficient search across a heterogeneous IoT estate.
solution_summary: Wattsense chose MongoDB Atlas as the data platform behind its connected-building service so one engineering team could manage device configurations, metadata, and time-series telemetry without stitching together multiple fragile systems. Atlas's document model stores large, deeply nested building and device configurations, while the aggregation framework is used to target and process specific data inside nested arrays. When native time series collections became available, Wattsense collapsed a separate SQL time-series stack into MongoDB as well, leaving Atlas to manage roughly 600GB of physical data and 1TB of logical data in one place. Atlas also scales capacity up and down automatically as demand changes, which lets Wattsense ingest parallel data from legacy equipment and LoRaWAN sensors across Europe without downtime. The result is a simpler architecture that supports plug-and-play building connectivity, Terraform-based infrastructure management, and future Atlas Search adoption.
